summary: Embedding header ordering heuristic causing rerank variance and intermittent p95 latency in multi-region bursts
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports inconsistent rerank results and spikes in p95 latency when calling the embeddings endpoint followed by rerank, observed only on dedicated tenancy in us-east and intermittently in eu-west. Impact: Search results reorderings and tail latency spikes causing visible UX regressions for AsteriaHealth users. Environment: Dedicated tenancy, heavy concurrent mix of 1-32 item embed batches; requests originate from two client SDK versions (1.4.0 and 1.5.2) using multi-part embedding upload.

Observed:
- Intermittent rerank top-k order changes (non-deterministic) across otherwise identical payloads.
- Rerank p95 increases from ~200ms to 1.6s during bursts.
- Traces show repeated retransmits and occasional fallback to CPU quant path during affected windows.

Expected: Deterministic top-k ordering for identical inputs and stable p95 latency under normal load.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Use AsteriaHealth test keys against embeddings endpoint in us-east with mixed-size batches (client SDK 1.5.2).
2) Send 400 concurrent requests with multipart payloads containing metadata header X-Client-Embed-Order set to "client" or omitted randomly.
3) Immediately call rerank endpoint with the returned embedding IDs.
4) Observe ordering variance across repeated runs and p95 latency on rerank.

Relevant logs/traces:
- Example trace ids: trace-us-20260310-5f2a, trace-eu-20260311-9c7b.
- Proxy logs (us-east): "[envoy] rewrite header X-Embed-Order=proxy-inserted for request id=5f2a"
- Embeddings service batching log: "batcher: observed chunk_order mismatch, invoking ordering-heuristic v2"
- Reranker warning: "candidate_alignment: mismatch_count=3, falling back to relaxed-match-mode"

Immediate impact: Customer-facing search relevance regressions and increased cost due to CPU fallbacks.

Batcher's ordering heuristic reorders chunks if header present to 'proxy-inserted' which can flip normalization path selection. Assigned to embeddings-service to harden validation and to proxy team for rollback.

investigation_notes: Envoy header rewrite introduced on 2026-03-09 in canary (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/proxy/pull/4789). Rule unconditionally added X-Embed-Order when content-type is multipart/form-data.

Embeddings service batcher relies on explicit client-provided ordering header to decide whether to preserve client chunk order or to normalize by arrival timestamp. When header is injected by proxy, heuristic selected 'preserve' path which mismatched the actual client chunk sequence for some SDK versions.

Mismatch caused occasional use of quantization CPU fallback path: heuristic toggled normalization that changed embedding dtype/shape assumptions, triggering a conversion path with higher latency and slight vector orientation perturbation leading to rerank top-k variance.

Affected traffic mostly on dedicated hosts during burst windows where proxy canary was active (us-east full rollout partial; eu-west partial). Regression window aligns with proxy rule deployment times and customer reports.

SRE rollback of the Envoy rule reduced incidents in us-east; eu-west rollback in progress. Embeddings-service PR to ignore injected X-Embed-Order and validate sequence checksums prepared (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/embeddings-service/pull/233).
resolution:
Temporary: Rolled back the Envoy header-rewrite rule from canaries in us-east and eu-west (2026-03-11). Confirmed AsteriaHealth's rerank ordering and p95 latency returned to baseline in our integration tests.
Permanent: Merged a fix in embeddings-service to validate chunk sequence checksums and ignore non-signed/injected X-Embed-Order headers (PR #233). Added a proxy integration test to prevent header injection for chunked embed uploads.
Customer communication: Notified AsteriaHealth of rollback and planned fix; provided link to follow-up postmortem and ETA for patch (ETA: 2026-03-15 for full rollout).
Follow-ups: Add canary gating for header-rewrite rules, add unit/integration tests for multipart header handling, update runbook to check for header rewrites during latency regressions.
